extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors preparing biomedical manuscripts for journal submission
extracted.subtask_description: Help authors identify and apply the correct reporting guideline (e.g., CONSORT, PRISMA, STROBE) for a biomedical study design, and follow practical checklist workflow steps to avoid submission errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting guidelines are structured checklists that tell you what information must appear in a manuscript for your study design. They don't tell you how to do research; they tell you how to describe it completely so others can evaluate and replicate it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use guidelines to ensure completeness and reproducibility; journals commonly require them at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision matrix: map study design to checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Map the study design to the right checklist without guessing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with the study design, match the framework, then move into the official checklist source; use the decision matrix when unsure which checklist applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: EQUATOR Network as authoritative source
rubrics_metrics.description: The EQUATOR Network maintains the largest database of reporting guidelines for health research (500+ guidelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your study type isn't covered by the core 12, use EQUATOR to find the appropriate guideline (e.g., COREQ for qualitative, GRAMMS for mixed-methods). Use the EQUATOR reporting-guideline selector tool when unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials — randomized controlled trials (RCTs). The 2010 checklist has 25 items covering design, analysis, and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gold standard for parallel-group RCTs; many extensions (cluster, crossover, non-inferiority, pragmatic, pilot/feasibility, N-of-1, social/psychological interventions). Mandatory or strongly recommended at NEJM, JAMA, Lancet, BMJ, and most clinical journals. Download official checklist from consort-statement.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses — systematic reviews and meta-analyses. PRISMA 2020 checklist has 27 items covering search, screening, extraction, risk of bias, and synthesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes extensions (PRISMA-P, PRISMA-IPD, PRISMA-NMA, PRISMA-DTA, PRISMA-Equity, PRISMA-Abstract). Required at most journals publishing systematic reviews, e.g., Lancet, BMJ, JAMA Network, Cochrane. Download from prisma-statement.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology — observational studies (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional). A 22-item checklist with versions for each design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Widely used in epidemiology, public health, and clinical medicine. Extensions include STROBE-NutriMed, STROBE-ME, STROME-ID. Recommended by Lancet, BMJ, JAMA, PLOS Medicine.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRIVE
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal Research: Reporting of In Vivo Experiments (ARRIVE 2.0) — animal (in vivo) research. A 21-item checklist aimed at improving reproducibility of preclinical animal studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates 'essential' and 'recommended' items. Required or recommended by Nature, Science, Cell Press journals, and most preclinical journals. See arriveguidelines.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: CARE
rubrics_metrics.description: CAse REport — case reports and case series. A 13-item checklist addressing timeline, patient perspective, diagnostic and therapeutic interventions, and follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required at BMJ Case Reports and recommended at many journals (JAMA, Lancet) that publish case reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for Reporting Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (STARD 2015) — diagnostic accuracy studies. A 30-item checklist for studies evaluating performance of a diagnostic test or biomarker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential for translational work in precision medicine, imaging, and lab diagnostics. STARD-AI extension exists for AI/ML diagnostic studies. Recommended by Radiology, JAMA, Lancet, Nature Medicine.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials — clinical trial protocols (not results). A 33-item checklist for reporting trial protocols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works alongside CONSORT (protocol vs results). Required by WHO trial registration and used by journals publishing trial protocols (e.g., BMJ, Trials).

rubrics_metrics.name: TRIPOD
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent Reporting of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis — prediction model studies (development, validation, updating). A 22-item checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical for clinical risk scores and AI diagnostic tools. TRIPOD+AI extension released 2024 for ML models. Increasingly required at BMJ, Lancet Digital Health, Nature Medicine.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards (CHEERS 2022) — health economic evaluations (cost-effectiveness, cost-benefit). A 28-item checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required when submitting HTAs or cost-effectiveness analyses; commonly required at Value in Health, BMJ, Lancet, and health economics journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: SQUIRE
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for Quality Improvement Reporting Excellence (SQUIRE 2.0) — quality improvement and patient safety studies. A 19-item checklist for reporting QI work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for interventions aimed at improving healthcare delivery, safety culture, or patient outcomes. Required at BMJ Quality & Safety, JAMA Network Open (QI studies), Joint Commission Journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOOSE
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta-analysis Of Observational Studies in Epidemiology — meta-analyses of observational (non-randomized) studies. A 35-item checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct from PRISMA (which covers systematic reviews/meta-analyses of RCTs and broader reviews); recommended at JAMA and epidemiology journals; particularly relevant for nutritional and environmental health research.

rubrics_metrics.name: RECORD
rubrics_metrics.description: REporting of studies Conducted using Observational Routinely-collected health Data — studies using routinely collected health data (EHR, claims, registries). An extension of STROBE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers EHR and administrative database studies; increasingly relevant as EHR-based research scales up. Recommended at JAMIA and clinical informatics journals. Often used alongside STROBE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which guideline applies — quick mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: If your study is an RCT use CONSORT; systematic reviews/meta-analyses use PRISMA; meta-analyses of observational studies use MOOSE; cohort/case-control/cross-sectional use STROBE; case reports use CARE; diagnostic accuracy studies use STARD; trial protocols use SPIRIT; prediction models use TRIPOD; animal research use ARRIVE; health economic evaluations use CHEERS; quality improvement use SQUIRE; EHR/claims/registry studies use RECORD (+ STROBE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some manuscripts need more than one guideline (e.g., systematic review of diagnostic accuracy studies: PRISMA + PRISMA-DTA). Use the decision matrix and EQUATOR when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Download the checklist early
rubrics_metrics.description: Download the checklist at the start of writing, not after. Some items (blinding procedures, randomization details, allocation concealment) require documentation that's easier to describe while it's fresh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat checklists as requirements to collect information during study conduct; retrofitting information after data collection can be impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Go item by item and locate content
rubrics_metrics.description: For each checklist item, confirm where in the manuscript the required information appears and note the page and section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many journals ask you to submit the checklist with page numbers filled in for every item; fill those in to avoid editors assuming omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly mark not-applicable items
rubrics_metrics.description: If a checklist item doesn't apply to your study, state so explicitly rather than leaving it blank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a short reason (e.g., 'N/A: no blinding was possible given the intervention design') because blank items look like omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit the completed checklist as a supplementary file
rubrics_metrics.description: Most journals require the completed checklist as a supplementary file, not part of the main manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check author instructions for required format; some journals have their own version of the checklist in the submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common submission mistakes to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Three practical mistakes that trigger avoidable friction: (1) waiting until submission week to identify the checklist, (2) leaving items blank instead of marking N/A with reasons, (3) submitting the checklist without page references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address these early in the workflow (download early, fill items with locations or N/A, include page numbers) to prevent desk rejection or return-to-author requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal requirement and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Most major journals now require specific reporting checklists at submission; submitting without the right one can trigger immediate desk rejection or a return-to-author request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm journal-specific requirements (some journals mandate particular extensions) and pair checklist selection with journal submission specs (file formats, abstract requirements, supplements).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use pre-submission checklist and submission-readiness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a pre-submission checklist after picking the reporting framework to ensure the rest of the submission package is ready. Use a submission-readiness check when you already have a manuscript and need a draft-specific signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair checklist selection with journal-specific file, abstract, and supplement requirements; move to data-sharing requirements when the checklist implies a formal data-availability statement or repository plan.
